purpose: Trace the primary-source lineage for the glucose-binding macrocycle used in NNC2215 and determine whether the references resolve the public model residue graph.

sources.title: Glucose-sensitive insulin with attenuation of hypoglycaemia
sources.specific_evidence: The paper identifies the glucose-binding macrocycle as its cited prior receptor, describes a roof propyl azide coupled by triazole formation to the B29 Lys alkyne linker, and provides a numbered chemical structure for the roof propyl azide in Extended Data Figure 8i. The SI provides its synthesis and NMR characterization.

sources.title: A biomimetic receptor for glucose
sources.specific_evidence: The supporting information includes synthesis and characterization of receptor 2 and a modelling section. Its free-receptor calculation uses a nonacarboxylate D surrogate because the full receptor structure caused software errors; results are figures and methods rather than machine-readable coordinates.

interpretation.notes: These sources materially improve the chemical provenance for the macrocycle scaffold and roof linker. They do not, by themselves, assign every atom in the model-built NNC2215 PDBs to an authoritative atom-mapped graph or validate the B1/B29 conjugate topology and force-field parameters. The 2019 receptor model is a related precursor/reference, not the complete NNC2215 conjugate.

next_validation_step: Build a candidate atom-mapped graph from the 2024 numbered roof-azide scheme, synthesis/SI, and the cited receptor structure; map it to the public PDB coordinates; then check total formula, valence, stereochemistry, linker bonds, and open/closed consistency before parameterization.
